papers.title: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Interactive game world models separate executable world evolution from visual generation, using video models to render engine-provided scene representations into detailed observations. During sustained gameplay, however, existing generative renderers struggle to follow changing conditions while preserving visual continuity across diverse proxies and target styles. We therefore introduce ContextRenderer, an autoregressive video diffusion framework designed for both dynamic conditioning and cross-proxy generalization. It couples Dynamic-Context Learning (DCL) for chunk-level interaction supervision with Recurrent History Compression (RHC) to follow condition updates while preserving visual continuity within a bounded token budget. Across proxy representations, Cross-Representation Flow Alignment (CRFA) connects proxy reconstruction with appearance and interaction variation through a shared high-fidelity reconstruction. WorldPrism, our interaction-centric dataset constructed from agent-built worlds, AAA gameplay, and open-source videos, supplies the corresponding renderings and chunk-level annotations for these learning tasks. Experiments on GWM-Bench and Solar-Bench show improved reconstruction and visual quality, while qualitative results demonstrate minute-long interactive rendering under changing prompts and subject references. Project page: https://rainzor.github.io/contextrenderer/

papers.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
papers.abstract: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.
papers.summary_cn: 论文提出 ScaleWorld，一个使用单一共享骨干网络同时完成低分辨率流式世界预测和高分辨率流式细化的因果视频模型。模型先逐块生成低分辨率视频，再利用同一模型将其细化为高分辨率结果；预测与细化分别维护较长的低分辨率清晰历史和较短的高分辨率噪声前向历史。训练上先分别优化预测和细化专家，再通过 TA-OPD 将两种能力整合到共享学生模型中。实验显示，该方法在保持原生世界预测能力和高分辨率生成质量的同时，减少模型权重占用，并通过复用噪声前向 KV 状态将细化生成速度提升约 2 倍；共享部署的峰值 GPU 内存降低 21.1%。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出共享因果世界模型，在同一骨干网络中实现流式低分辨率世界预测与流式高分辨率细化，并保持原生低分辨率预测路径独立可用。2. 设计非对称因果记忆：世界预测保留较长的低分辨率清晰 KV 历史，细化保留较短的高分辨率噪声前向 KV 历史，从而避免额外的高分辨率历史构建计算。3. 提出任务非对称在线策略蒸馏（TA-OPD），先分别训练预测和细化专家，再依据各任务不同的采样与历史策略，通过局部速度匹配将能力整合到共享学生模型。4. 通过受控实验验证了共享权重、非对称记忆和噪声前向 KV 复用在生成质量、推理速度及 GPU 内存方面的效果。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与视频生成和视频扩散高度相关，核心对象是因果视频扩散世界模型。它直接涉及动作或相机控制条件下的视觉世界生成，并采用逐块自回归、因果、流式生成机制，适合持续生成长视频。其低分辨率预测到高分辨率细化的共享骨干设计与高分辨率视频生成有关；TA-OPD 面向多能力蒸馏，非对称因果状态和 KV 缓存复用则对应实时生成、缓存复用和计算效率优化。实验中模型以 12 FPS 的高分辨率流式配置运行，噪声前向历史使细化阶段生成速度从 26.7 FPS 提升至 53.3 FPS，并在端到端部署中保持 11.94 FPS。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文正文明确显示，统一模型的能力保留并不完全均衡：其原生世界预测的一致性和物理维度略低于预测专家，细化的时间残差在噪声前向历史下也有小幅增加。共享骨干虽然减少了权重和峰值 GPU 内存，但两种角色的 KV 缓存仍需同时保留，因此 KV 占用没有因权重共享而减少。高分辨率细化实验主要基于固定的低分辨率视频，部分外部基线使用不同空间评测协议，直接比较存在限制。论文提到限制在附录 E 中讨论，但所提供文本未包含该附录的具体内容；其余未明确说明的局限为：论文未明确说明。
papers.abstract_cn: 高分辨率生成能够使视频世界模型呈现细粒度的场景结构与纹理，但直接生成高分辨率视频会带来巨大的计算和内存开销。我们提出了 ScaleWorld，这是一种因果视频模型，在单一共享骨干网络中统一了低分辨率世界预测与高分辨率细化。ScaleWorld 通过细化自身的预测结果生成高分辨率世界视频，无需独立的细化模型。对于每个视频块，共享骨干网络首先完成低分辨率预测，然后以该预测为条件执行一次高分辨率细化。为支持高效的流式生成，我们维护独立的因果状态：预测使用较长的低分辨率历史，细化使用较短的高分辨率历史。为解决蒸馏过程中的任务干扰问题，我们将专家模型优化与能力整合分离，并提出任务非对称在线策略蒸馏（TA-OPD）。该方法根据各自的采样策略和历史策略，通过局部速度匹配，将专门化教师模型的预测与细化行为迁移到共享学生模型中。大量实验表明，ScaleWorld 在实现高质量世界生成的同时，提升了计算和内存效率。

papers.title: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency
papers.abstract: Controllable streaming video generation offers a promising route toward interactive game simulation, yet existing methods remain far from practical gameplay. They often fail to jointly achieve high visual fidelity, high frame rates, and low interaction latency, resulting in poor responsiveness and degraded user experience. We present Streaming-AAA, a new paradigm for controllable infinite generation of AAA-quality game videos. Our system generates 1080p gameplay videos at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end latency interaction on merely NVIDIA A800 GPUs, while supporting long-horizon play without severe temporal degradation or collapse. Streaming-AAA is built upon three key designs. First, we redesign the VAE architecture for efficient high-resolution decoding, enabling real-time synthesis at 1080p. Second, we pretrain the diffusion model using diffusion forcing and significantly extend the temporal training horizon, allowing the model to capture long-term dependencies and maintain persistent memory. Third, we perform post-training distillation and memory compression to improve inference efficiency while retaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Experiments show that Streaming-AAA substantially improves visual fidelity, frame rate, latency, and long-term stability over prior controllable video generation approaches, enabling a significantly more playable experience for interactive AAA game video generation.
papers.summary_cn: Streaming-AAA 面向可控的无限长 AAA 游戏视频生成，重点解决高分辨率、高帧率、低延迟和长时稳定性难以兼顾的问题。系统使用重新设计的高分辨率因果视频 VAE、分解空间与时间建模的 3D UNet 潜空间扩散模型，以及支持动作、天气、时间等条件的统一跨注意力机制。通过 Diffusion Forcing 长上下文预训练、DMD 训练后蒸馏、混合长短期 KV 缓存和并行化 teacher-forcing 推理，模型在《原神》数据上实现 1080p、约 43 FPS 和约 198 毫秒理论端到端延迟，并展示了最长一小时连续生成的稳定性。论文同时指出，该方法主要针对单一游戏训练，跨游戏、跨画风和跨机制的泛化能力有限。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 Streaming-AAA，可控地生成无限时长的 AAA 游戏视频，并同时达到 1080p、约 43 FPS、约 198 毫秒理论端到端延迟和较稳定的长时滚动生成。 2. 设计高分辨率因果视频 VAE，采用 16 倍空间压缩和 Pixel Shuffle 解码，以降低 1080p 实时解码开销并保留细节。 3. 构建因子化 3D UNet 潜空间扩散骨干，将空间纹理、时间动态和条件控制分离建模，并支持动作、天气、时间和帧率等多模态条件。 4. 采用逐帧独立噪声调度的 Diffusion Forcing 预训练，以及面向清洁历史上下文和固定推理步数的 DMD 训练后对齐，以缩小训练与流式推理分布差异、提升长时稳定性。 5. 提出混合长短期 KV 缓存，仅保存 30 个令牌，并结合并行化 teacher-forcing 推理，降低无限流式生成的计算和延迟成本。 6. 构建自动化分布式数据采集系统，收集约 2.2 万段、约 4000 万帧的 1080p 游戏视频及动作、天气和时间标注。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它将扩散视频生成直接用于动作条件的交互式视觉世界模型和闭环游戏模拟：模型根据历史画面、玩家动作及环境条件因果地预测后续视频，并支持连续控制和长时滚动。Diffusion Forcing、长上下文训练、DMD 蒸馏、因子化时空注意力、稀疏混合 KV 缓存和两步去噪分别对应长视频生成、实时生成、蒸馏加速、稀疏注意力与缓存复用等方向。其 1080p、43 FPS、约 198 毫秒理论延迟及一小时连续游玩实验，直接体现了面向实时闭环交互的系统目标。不过，论文主要验证于《原神》单一游戏，尚不能证明其对通用视觉世界模型或多游戏环境的泛化能力。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，方法主要针对单一游戏标题进行设计和优化，训练数据来自单一游戏，因此对未见过的游戏环境、艺术风格和游戏机制的泛化能力有限；构建无需逐游戏微调的通用游戏生成模型仍是开放问题。此外，论文报告的 198 毫秒延迟是理论计算延迟，排除了网络传输和编解码开销。数据中的天气和时间信息由视觉语言模型从画面估计，而非直接读取游戏引擎，可能带来标注误差。论文未明确说明跨多个游戏、不同硬件平台以及更复杂动作空间下的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 可控的流式视频生成是实现交互式游戏模拟的一条有前景的途径，但现有方法距离实用游戏体验仍相距甚远。它们通常难以同时实现高视觉保真度、高帧率和低交互延迟，因而导致响应性差、用户体验下降。我们提出 Streaming-AAA，一种面向 AAA 级游戏视频的可控无限生成新范式。我们的系统仅使用 NVIDIA A800 GPU，即可生成 1080p、43 FPS 的游戏视频，并实现 198 毫秒的端到端交互延迟，同时支持长时段游玩而不会出现严重的时间退化或崩溃。Streaming-AAA 建立在三项关键设计之上。首先，我们重新设计了 VAE 架构，以实现高效的高分辨率解码，从而支持 1080p 实时合成。其次，我们使用 Diffusion Forcing 对扩散模型进行预训练，并显著延长时间训练跨度，使模型能够捕获长期依赖并维持持久记忆。第三，我们进行训练后蒸馏和记忆压缩，以提升推理效率，同时保留视觉质量和时间一致性。实验表明，与此前的可控视频生成方法相比，Streaming-AAA 在视觉保真度、帧率、延迟和长期稳定性方面均有显著提升，从而实现了更具可玩性的交互式 AAA 游戏视频生成体验。

papers.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
papers.abstract: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.
papers.summary_cn: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties.

papers.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control
papers.abstract: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding. Purely visual interfaces may lack analytical dynamics, structured states, or explicit collision geometry, requiring internal prediction of action-conditioned process risk. We propose Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) for frozen Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Rather than relying on static state features that cannot distinguish candidate plans sharing an observation, RTS unrolls action-conditioned future latent prefixes in the frozen world model and trains a lightweight risk head with process-violation supervision. To intervene selectively while preserving safe nominal behavior, RTS uses the same predicted prefix-risk criterion as both the search trigger gate and hard feasibility gate: safe nominal plans execute directly, whereas alarms trigger local Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) search to minimize nominal deviation within the feasible set. To prevent isotropic Euclidean minimal modification from shrinking obstacle-directed actions into zero-amplitude stalling, we introduce an amplitude-preserving metric $d_{\mathrm{AP}}$ that retains tangential progression while maintaining a unique zero at the nominal plan. Under unified gating and this unique-zero condition, bypassing safe-state search yields closed-loop trajectories strictly identical to every-step same-kernel search. Evaluated under a process-safety benchmark and Safe Arrival Rate (SAR) metric across five tasks, RTS improves SAR over Direct by 12.67--41.67 percentage points on navigation and articulated control and +2.08/+4.17 pp on Cube/PushT boundary cohorts, maintaining 100% action identity with every-step search while cutting controller time by 17.71%--70.41% across 1,968 paired trajectories.
papers.summary_cn: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding.

papers.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
papers.abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.
papers.summary_cn: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference.

papers.title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.
papers.summary_cn: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media.
papers.contribution_cn: To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales.

papers.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.
papers.summary_cn: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running.

papers.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
papers.abstract: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop. The graph supports joint saving and restoration of rules and world states, while dynamic object binding grounds rule-specified entities in visual instances and uses stored states to constrain generation from their first appearance. We further introduce object attribute state replacement and counterfactual reconstruction training, enabling accurate attribute control and compatible appearance and motion changes while limiting interference with unrelated content. We develop an automated data collection and annotation pipeline using GTA-V and Habitat to construct RuleVerse, a dataset of rule-driven interactions with detailed state and event annotations, including cases where rules take effect before affected objects become visible. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRuler in preserving rule-state consistency across saving and loading and accurately realizing rule outcomes on designated objects and attributes.

papers.title: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Video diffusion transformers reuse key--value (KV) caches across denoising steps, which quickly becomes a bottleneck for long video generation. We find that quantizing temporally distant cache vectors leads to a large range and high quantization error, but that nearby video tokens in the KV-cache share a persistent pattern per channel. These patterns also vary across videos, motivating rotations that are adapted to each video's unique cache. We propose Temporal Rotation Quantization (TRQ), a method that rotates frames in the cache that are adjacent in time before quantization. For each block of temporally adjacent cache vectors, TRQ fits an orthogonal transform that maps the block's per-channel means to a vector that is close to a constant across channels. To keep the quantization format lightweight, we parameterize this rotation as a tree of $2 \times 2$ planar rotations, each stored with only two bits, followed by a fixed Hadamard transform shared across all blocks. The rotations are fit without gradients or changes to model weights, and we prove that a simple greedy fit is globally optimal for our 'mean-flattening' objective. The transforms are fit online for each new video, and we release fused Triton kernels to make this process efficient at inference. At 2-bit precision and matched compression, TRQ improves VBench subject consistency over the state-of-the-art method QVG from 90.38 to 92.02 on LongCat-Video-13B and from 86.33 to 87.61 on HY-WorldPlay-8B, as well as improving other metrics.
papers.summary_cn: Video diffusion transformers reuse key--value (KV) caches across denoising steps, which quickly becomes a bottleneck for long video generation.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose Temporal Rotation Quantization (TRQ), a method that rotates frames in the cache that are adjacent in time before quantization.
